long_biography.plain_text:
The Constitution divides the U.S. federal government into legislative, executive and judicial branches. Congress drafts legislation and oversees federal spending; the executive branch implements and enforces federal law through the presidency, departments and agencies; federal courts interpret and apply law. Checks and balances allow each branch to limit actions by the others.

The institution continues even as presidents, legislators, judges and civil servants change. It administers national policy and public services within powers granted by the Constitution, while powers not assigned to the federal government remain with states or the people. The label USA Government therefore denotes the federal governmental system collectively, not any officeholder, department, agency or employee.
